answer: Randomized challenge quorum. Each epoch, a verifiable random function draws a fresh quorum from a registered vault of participants, and only that quorum may sign off on new identities. An attacker cannot precompute which vertex in the registry will be sampled, so it must maintain live, responsive presence across the whole membership rather than spin up cheap clones right before a check. Every relic of past participation stays auditable, and the per-identity cost becomes continuous infrastructure upkeep, not a one-time fee.
